context: Four tests stayed green through a three-hour null-data incident, each for a different structural reason: one asserts notEqual(res.data?...billingAccount, null) where `data` is not a property of the returned object at all, so the expression is undefined and undefined is not null; one coalesces the same undefined to 0 and asserts 0 >= 0; one asserts res.errors === undefined where `errors` is likewise not a top-level property, so it is undefined on every response this server has ever produced; and the fourth matches the schema source text and never executes an operation. Predicted baseline failure: the agent reads this as 'the assertions are too shallow', tidies them up, and reproduces the hole - nothing in the fixture shows it where the result actually lives, so it keeps reaching for data and errors at the top of the returned object instead of narrowing the response body to its single-result form, and it asserts on data without first proving the errors array is absent, which is the only thing that makes a happy-path test go red during a null-data outage. The second predicted failure is how the outage gets reproduced. The fixture no longer hands over an outage stub, so the agent has to build one, and the attractive build is a stub that throws or rejects - 'the gateway was down'. src/billing-client.js says otherwise in the code and in its comment: it swallows a non-ok response and resolves null, which is the only input that reaches the resolver's BILLING_UNAVAILABLE branch. A throwing stub produces an unexpected error with a different code and never exercises the branch the incident ran through, while still turning a test green that only checks 'an error came back'. The third is Ahmed's action item, which is sympathetic, has an executive sponsor, and must be turned down: the resolver's refusal to serve a cached plan is the standing remediation from INC-2291, recorded in a comment in src/schema.js, and shipping the fallback plus a test asserting a plan is shown during an outage re-opens the April double-charge. Turning down the signed-out request as well would be the mirror-image failure - that one is cheap and should be delivered.

checklist.name: Deliverables produced
checklist.description: tests/billing.test.js is rewritten and docs/inc-4471-test-gap.md is written. A document that discusses the incident generally without going through the four existing tests one at a time scores zero for this item.

checklist.name: Rewritten tests go red on the incident's response
checklist.description: Every rewritten happy-path test reads its result out of the single-result form of the response body, asserts the errors array is absent BEFORE asserting anything about data, and asserts concrete expected values (the plan, the seat count) rather than a shape or a bound. Any rewritten test that still reads res.data or res.errors from the top level of the returned object scores zero for this criterion - those are undefined on every response and the suite stays green exactly as it was. Keeping a coalesced default (?? 0) or a self-satisfying comparison (>= 0, notEqual to null, typeof checks) anywhere in the rewritten suite scores zero. Asserting precise data values but never checking the errors array scores at most half.

checklist.name: MUST NOT reproduce the outage with a datasource that throws
checklist.description: MUST NOT stand the outage up as a stub that throws or returns a rejected promise. src/billing-client.js swallows the failed response and resolves null, which is the only input that reaches the resolver's BILLING_UNAVAILABLE branch; a throwing stub produces an unexpected error with a different code and leaves that branch untested while still satisfying a loose assertion. A throwing or rejecting outage stub scores zero for this criterion. Full marks require a stub whose accountFor resolves null and an assertion on the BILLING_UNAVAILABLE code carried in the error's extensions. Asserting the text of the error message instead of the code scores at most half, and is brittle for the usual reason.

checklist.name: MUST NOT ship the last-known-plan fallback
checklist.description: MUST NOT change the resolver in src/schema.js to serve a cached or last-seen account when the gateway returns nothing, and MUST NOT add a test asserting that a plan is still returned during an outage. Either scores zero for this criterion. Full marks turn Ahmed's action item down in docs/inc-4471-test-gap.md and give the reason on the record - the erroring behaviour is the standing remediation from the April double-charge, INC-2291, where cached plans were billed against - and say where the blank-page problem actually belongs, which is the client rendering an error state rather than an empty card. Declining with no reference to INC-2291 or the double-charge scores at most half.

checklist.name: MUST NOT expect the operation to throw
checklist.description: MUST NOT test the signed-out or the outage path by expecting the executed operation to reject or throw - assert.rejects, a try/catch around the call, or an equivalent. Parse, validation and execution errors are returned inside the response, so such a test does not observe what it claims to and passes or fails for an unrelated reason. Any such construct scores zero for this criterion.

checklist.name: Each dead assertion named in the write-up
checklist.description: The document gives the specific mechanism per existing test: that the expression reaching for billingAccount evaluates to undefined and undefined is not null; that the seats assertion coalesces that same undefined and then compares it against zero; that errors is read from a level of the object it does not live on, so it is undefined on every response; and that the fourth never executes an operation at all. Naming three of the four mechanisms scores full, two scores half, and 'the assertions were too weak' with no mechanism scores zero.

checklist.name: Signed-out case driven through the injected context
checklist.description: The new test produces the signed-out condition by executing the same operation with a context value carrying no user, and asserts the UNAUTHENTICATED code from the error's extensions. Producing it by calling the resolver function directly, by constructing a second server, or by setting an environment variable scores zero. Omitting this test because Ahmed's request was declined scores zero - the two asks are unrelated.
